hints: Focus on what pH really measures, the concentration of H+ or OH- actually in solution, not just how much acid or base you started with.
Compare acid 1 and acid 2 at the same 0.1 mol dm-3 concentration, one gives pH 4 and the other gives pH 1, so think about which one fully splits into ions.
Check each statement in turn and ask whether solubility or degree of dissociation best explains the big pH difference.
walkthrough:
**Recall strong versus weak**

All four solutions have the same starting concentration, 0.1 mol dm-3. So any difference in pH must be due to how much they dissociate or ionise in water.

Strong acids and bases dissociate fully: $$\text{HNO}_3 \rightarrow \text{H}^+ + \text{NO}_3^-$$ $$\text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{Na}^+ + \text{OH}^-$$ Weak acids and bases dissociate only partly, setting up an equilibrium.

**Compare the two acids**

Acid 2, $\text{HNO}_3$, pH 1, is a strong acid. $[\text{H}^+] \approx 0.1$ mol dm-3, so pH = 1. Acid 1, $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H}$, pH 4, is a weak acid. Only a tiny fraction dissociates: $$\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H} \rightleftharpoons \text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2^- + \text{H}^+$$ So $[\text{H}^+]$ is much less than 0.1. The difference is strength of dissociation, not solubility.

**Compare the two bases and decide**

Base 2, $\text{NaOH}$, pH 14, is a strong base and gives full 0.1 mol dm-3 $\text{OH}^-$. Base 1, $\text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2$, pH 11, is a weak base and gives much less $\text{OH}^-$. So statement 2 is true and statement 3 is true, while statement 1 is false. That leaves statements 2 and 3 only.

options.A: This option claims statements 1, 2 and 3 are all correct. Statements 2 and 3 are correct, but statement 1 is wrong because both acids are soluble at 0.1 mol dm-3. The lower pH is due to complete dissociation of the strong acid, not greater solubility.
options.B: This option claims only statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 2 is correct, but statement 1 is incorrect for the reason above, and it wrongly leaves out statement 3 which correctly describes weak versus strong dissociation.
options.C: This option correctly selects statements 2 and 3 only. Base 2 fully dissociates so [OH-] is higher than for weak base 1, and acid 1 is weak so it dissociates far less than strong acid 2, giving fewer H+ ions and a higher pH.
options.D: This option claims only statement 3 is correct. Statement 3 is indeed true, but this choice is incomplete because statement 2 is also true. Weak base 1 produces much less OH- than strong base 2 at the same concentration.
